title: Publish a fair value only, never a fake market price
problem: The brief asks to originate lines. There is no official source of market prices in this repo, so any displayed price that looks like a market quote would be invented.
proposal: Output one number per game: our fair-value probability, with an explicit uncertainty band and a timestamp. Display the market price column as blank until the user supplies a benchmark feed.
evidence: data/sources.tsv S03 — official standings supply team scoring, but no official price feed was found.
options: Fair value only, price column blank and labelled. (Recommended)
Fair value plus a user-supplied price feed.
Wait for a price feed before publishing anything.
recommendation: A. A blank, labelled column is honest and costs nothing. Option C delays all work on the strength of a data source that was never promised.
impact: Protects the whole site from being built on an invented number.

title: Grade every strategy on calibration first, profit second
problem: Ranking strategies by win rate or units won rewards luck. Over a few dozen bets the noise band is wider than any realistic edge.
proposal: Make calibration the primary gate: bucket predictions by stated probability and check that the realised hit rate matches. Rank on calibration error and sample size, and show profit only after the sample gate is met.
evidence: data/questions.json Q09, Q10 — the season is 18 weeks and Week 10 is in progress (S05).
options: Profit-primary ranking with a minimum sample gate.
Rank on both and display them side by side without combining.
recommendation: A, with C as a display layer. Profit-first ranking will surface a lucky strategy in week one and destroy the credibility of the board.
impact: Turns the leaderboard from a lottery into a measurement.

title: Freeze predictions before kickoff with a cryptographic seal
problem: A strategy record is worthless if a prediction can be edited after the result is known. Without a seal, no reader can distinguish a genuine forecast from hindsight.
proposal: Write each prediction to a timestamped file before kickoff and record a SHA-256 hash of the prediction set. Publish the hashes. After the game, publish the results; the hash proves the forecast did not change.
evidence: data/questions.json Q02, Q12.
options: Hash-sealed prediction log committed before kickoff. (Recommended)
recommendation: A. It is nearly free, and it is the single cheapest thing that makes the leaderboard credible.
impact: Converts claims into an auditable record.

title: Split the backup-deficiency feature into 'observed absence' and 'derived depth'
problem: The brief wants 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacements tracked. There is no league-wide official depth chart (S13 returns 404), no official snap-count feed in this repo, and club depth charts are self-labelled 'Unofficial' (S08).
proposal: Show two clearly separated tables. (1) Observed absence: straight from the official injury report, no inference. (2) Derived depth: built from roster status codes plus each club's own published depth chart, and labelled derived everywhere it appears.
evidence: data/sources.tsv S13 (404), S08 (club page titled 'Unofficial Depth Chart'), S07 (roster status codes), S01 (injury report).
reversibility: Reversible — the derived layer can be removed without touching the observed layer.
options: Two-layer build, observed and derived kept strictly separate. (Recommended)
Observed absence only; defer depth entirely.
Build derived depth and present it as if it were official.
recommendation: A. Option C is the trap: it would look like the most impressive feature on the site while being the least defensible.
impact: Delivers the requested feature without asserting something the sources cannot support.

title: Add a Flagged for Review page as a first-class section
problem: Irregularities and unverifiable values currently have nowhere to live. The alternative is quietly filling them in, which is exactly what the brief forbids.
proposal: A permanent page listing every unverified value, every 404 source, every cross-source contradiction, and every open question, each with the source link that was attempted and the date. Nothing is hidden and nothing is guessed.
evidence: data/sources.tsv S12-S14 (404s), data/questions.json Q08 (cross-source contradictions).
options: Dedicated page, always populated, never empty. (Recommended)
A footnote at the bottom of the home page.
Leave unreviewed items out of the site entirely.
recommendation: A. It is the mechanism that lets the rest of the site be trusted.
impact: Makes the honesty of the dataset visible instead of asserted.

title: Adopt walk-forward validation with a frozen, access-logged holdout
problem: Tuning and scoring on the same weeks produces an optimistic number that will not survive contact with future games.
proposal: Train on weeks 1..k, predict week k+1, roll forward. Never shuffle. Keep the final weeks in a separate frozen file and log every single time it is read.
evidence: data/questions.json Q12.
options: Strict walk-forward with a logged holdout. (Recommended)
recommendation: A. Option B leaks future information into the past in a sport with strong week-to-week drift.
impact: Prevents the most common way an in-house model exaggerates its own accuracy.

title: Start with team totals, and defer parlays until legs are individually validated
problem: The brief asks for single bets, parlays and prop combos at once. Parlays multiply variance, so a failed parlay does not reveal which leg was wrong, and props need player-level joint data this repo does not yet have.
proposal: Sequence the work: team-level single market first, then player props once player data exists, then 2-leg combos only after each leg independently clears its own gate, then correlation estimation.
evidence: data/questions.json Q01, Q11.
reversibility: Fully reversible — it is an ordering, not a removal.
options: All three product types in parallel.
recommendation: A. Option B is how projects end up with a parlay board backed by three unvalidated legs.
impact: Keeps every published number downstream of a validated one.

title: Require every strategy to beat a published naive baseline
problem: A model that only rediscovers 'the better team usually wins' looks skilful when compared to nothing.
proposal: Publish a named baseline, for example a points-differential rating from official season scoring. A strategy is only ranked if it beats that baseline out of sample.
evidence: data/sources.tsv S03 — official PF/PA for all 32 clubs.
options: Baseline shown for information but not required.
recommendation: A. Without it the leaderboard measures effort, not edge.
impact: Makes the leaderboard's ranking mean something.

title: Timestamp and never overwrite every injury snapshot
problem: The injury report changes several times a week. A single undated snapshot cannot support any claim about timing, and mixing snapshots introduces look-ahead bias.
proposal: One immutable file per capture, named by UTC timestamp. All analysis reads a specific snapshot and records which one.
evidence: data/sources.tsv S01; data/questions.json Q06.
options: Capture only once, at the end of the week.
recommendation: A. Option C discards the entire within-week signal, which is the only part that is not already in the closing price.
impact: Preserves the ability to ask timing questions later.

title: Make the site a static dashboard with no build step
problem: A build pipeline introduces a failure mode where the live site silently lags the repository.
proposal: Plain HTML, one stylesheet, small scripts that read the committed data files at load time. No bundler, no framework, no server. GitHub Pages serves the repository root directly.
evidence: GitHub Pages for this repository is already configured on the main branch root and reports a built status.
options: Static site generator with a build action.
recommendation: A. Nothing to break, nothing to version, and Pages serves it as-is.
impact: The published site cannot drift from the committed data.

title: Keep the leaderboard non-monetary until a legal review exists
problem: The brief asks for rewards. A prize pool turns a statistics page into something a gambling regulator may take an interest in, and the rules are jurisdiction-specific.
proposal: Rewards are ranking position and a badge. No money, no entry fee, no wagering, no odds. Record the legal question openly rather than answering it.
evidence: data/questions.json Q14.
risk: Low if adopted; high if ignored
recommendation: A. It delivers the requested competitive structure with none of the exposure.
impact: Keeps the project squarely informational.

title: Separate 'observed' from 'derived' in every table, visibly
problem: Mixing values read directly from a source with values computed from them makes the whole table unauditable.
proposal: Tag each row with its provenance: OBSERVED (read verbatim from a linked official page) or DERIVED (computed, with the formula stated). Blanks are never filled.
evidence: All data files in this repo.
options: Provenance documented in a separate methodology page only.
recommendation: A. A reader should never have to guess whether a number was read or computed.
impact: Makes line-by-line verification possible, which is what the brief asks for.

title: Expand depth coverage one club at a time, starting with a single worked example
problem: 32 clubs times their own depth chart format is a large, error-prone surface. Attempting all of it at once would produce 32 half-checked tables.
proposal: Ship one club fully worked and verified, with the matchup relevance explained, then expand club by club behind the same validation.
evidence: data/sources.tsv S08, S07; data/depth-kc.tsv.
options: One verified club first, then expand. (Recommended)
recommendation: A. It demonstrates the method end-to-end and keeps every published cell checkable.
impact: Proves the approach before scaling it.

title: Reconcile contradictions by publishing them, never by choosing silently
problem: Official pages disagree with each other in this dataset (a Rams defender's team attribution, and a Rams defender who appears both as active and as a non-participant).
proposal: Leave both values as captured, link both sources, and list the contradiction on the Flagged for Review page with a note that no resolution was applied.
evidence: data/questions.json Q08; data/sources.tsv S01, S10, S15.
options: Drop the player from the table.
recommendation: A. Any silent choice would be an unlogged inference, which is what the brief prohibits.
impact: Keeps the dataset honest and makes the source's own errors reviewable.

title: Add a one-page decision brief for each open question
problem: The open-questions list is long. A decision-maker reading twenty questions has no fast way to choose a path.
proposal: The Suggestions page groups each question with the options, the trade-off, a recommendation and the cost of being wrong, so a reviewer can approve or reject in one pass.
evidence: This file; data/questions.json.
recommendation: A. It is the difference between a list of worries and a set of choices.
impact: Makes the review step actually completable.

title: Choose a betting-price source before any market column or ROI is computed
problem: No official NFL source publishes betting prices. The price-snapshot store, the market columns and ROI are therefore blank (F18).
proposal: The owner names a price source. Until then the store stays empty and nothing on the site shows a market number.
evidence: data/price_snapshots.tsv (39 blank rows); data/model_lines.tsv (market columns blank); flagged F18.
risk: Medium (a third-party source that looks official would be a credibility risk)
options: Keep blank (no price source) until one is chosen. (Recommended while the decision is open.)
Owner supplies a licensed feed, labelled 'licensed, not official', with its terms recorded.
Accept the third-party nflverse closing lines as a labelled non-official source (already in data/raw/closing_lines.csv).
recommendation: A. Nothing should be computed against prices until the owner has chosen a source and its terms. Option C would make the ROI and the difference columns real, but would sit outside the brief's official-only rule.
impact: Decides whether the difference column and ROI can ever be filled.

title: Confirm the demotion-gate thresholds (G-14) before any strategy goes live
problem: The G-14 windows (100 bets to demote, 250 to re-promote) and the 95% lower-bound rule are proposals, not facts about football.
proposal: The owner accepts or changes the windows and the bound. The rule shape (exposure, sample, signal, CLV) stays as written.
evidence: engine/gates.py (demotion_decision, repromotion_decision); governance.html worked examples; tests/test_brief.py.
risk: Low while no strategy is live
options: Keep the proposed defaults (100 to demote, 250 to re-promote, 95% lower bound). (Recommended for a paper trial.)
Longer windows (250 to demote) to make demotion slower and less noisy.
Add a drawdown trigger, which needs an owner-supplied number.
recommendation: A. The defaults are the smallest honest windows the code supports. A drawdown number is a policy choice and should come from the owner.
impact: Sets how quickly a live strategy is returned to paper.

title: Re-read the official Week 1-9 pages game by game before any backtest is quoted
problem: Only Week 10 results were re-read per game from an official page. Weeks 1-9 are reconciled to the standings in aggregate only (F22).
proposal: Read the nine official week pages and compare every game row (a line-by-line check), recording the result in data/verification-brief.tsv.
evidence: data/results.tsv (137 rows); S50 (official week pages); F22.
options: Do the nine-page line-by-line check now. (Recommended.)
Accept aggregate reconciliation for now and label every backtest accordingly.
Drop Weeks 1-9 from the model inputs until they are verified.
recommendation: A. The backtest is only as good as its inputs, and the brief asks for line-by-line verification.
impact: Turns the results feed from aggregate-reconciled into per-game verified.

title: Decide whether any third-party-derived correlation may ever be shown
problem: Brief B6 says correlations come only from official numbers, with n shown. Every existing coefficient comes from the nflverse mirror, so all are withheld (F19).
proposal: The owner confirms the strict rule (withheld) or allows third-party values under a visible non-official label.
evidence: prop-correlations.html (withheld, n shown); measured.html (withdrawal banner); flagged F19.
risk: Medium if a third-party coefficient were used as a bet input
options: Keep withheld; no coefficient is published. (Recommended, and the brief's current rule.)
Show third-party coefficients with n and a 'non-official' label, and never use them to size a bet.
Find an official joint sample (for example official box scores) before computing any correlation.
recommendation: A. The brief is explicit. Option C is the right long-term path and needs a source that has not been found yet.
impact: Decides whether the correlation pages ever show a number.

title: Record opening prices at origination from Week 11 onward
problem: Every open cell in the price-snapshot store is blank because no historical opening-price source exists, and nothing is being recorded prospectively either.
proposal: The moment we publish our own line for a market, snapshot the market's opening number into the store (the fields and the validation already exist). Over time this manufactures the missing history at zero cost.
evidence: data/price_snapshots.json coverage: 0/56 open cells filled.
prerequisites: A captured market number at publication time (today: the pinned S47 feed)
recommendation: A. It starts closing GAP-01 prospectively at zero cost and cannot make anything worse.
impact: Opening cells fill from Week 11; open-to-close movement becomes measurable.

title: Purchase a licensed opening + closing line history
problem: Closing-line value (gate G-3), honest difference columns and historical backtests all need prices with clean provenance. Today's prices are third-party and flagged.
proposal: Buy or license a historical line feed covering the seasons we backtest, with open and close per market. This is the single purchase that unblocks the most gates.
evidence: G-3 is BLOCKED in engine/gates.py for want of prices; flag F23; question Q21.
recommendation: A if budget allows; B is the honest interim and is what runs now.
impact: G-3 becomes evaluable; difference columns stop carrying the third-party badge; backtests gain a defensible price basis.

title: Adopt the signal/staking split and the demotion gate as written competition rules
problem: Without the split, a lucky staking run ranks above good signal; without demotion, a live badge outlives the edge that earned it.
proposal: Rank on the signal block only (engine/backtest.py), report staking separately, and demote live strategies to paper on any of D1/D2/D3 (engine/demotion.py, gate G-14).
evidence: data/leaderboard_signal_staking.json re-ranks the 16 computed-layer strategies on signal; flag F28 publishes the thresholds.
reversibility: Rules can be amended between seasons
options: Rank on a blended signal+staking score.
recommendation: A. Blending re-opens the door the requirement exists to close.
impact: Lucky staking cannot mask bad signal; decaying strategies return to paper automatically.

title: Capture official injury and depth snapshots weekly
problem: One week of injury captures exists. Correlation C-A4 (availability vs margin) is stuck at n=1, and replacement depth only reflects Week 10.
proposal: Extend the weekly refresh workflow to capture the official injury report and club depth charts each week of the season, appending to the verified feed.
evidence: data/correlations_official.json C-A4 row (n=1, blank); .github/workflows/refresh.yml already runs weekly.
recommendation: A. The correlation register's n is the decision-quality bottleneck.
impact: C-A4 becomes computable; replacement depth tracks the whole season.

title: Decide the market-price publication policy (F-18 / F-11)
problem: The brief both demands the market-line column and forbids unconfirmed values. The sprint resolved it provisionally with a THIRD_PARTY badge; the owner should ratify or overrule.
proposal: Pick one of three policies and record it: (A) publish third-party prices with badge + flag [current], (B) strict blank on every market cell, (C) licensed feed then publish as sourced.
evidence: flags F23/F11; question Q23; amended footer describing the badge.
recommendation: A until C is affordable, then C. B if the no-price promise must hold absolutely.
impact: Sets what the line board, snapshots and leaderboard are allowed to display.

title: Unify the leaderboard wording across the two site layers (F-19)
problem: The root Leaderboard page said no backtest existed anywhere in the repository while the computed layer publishes 16 backtested strategies over third-party data.
proposal: Point the root page at the computed layer explicitly: plan-level strategies (official data only) and computed-layer backtests (third-party, flagged) are two different registers and should say so.
evidence: flag F24; strategies.html; docs/pages/leaderboard.html.
options: Point root page at computed layer. (Recommended)
recommendation: A. Both registers are useful; the error was the word 'anywhere'.
impact: A reader stops being told two contradictory things.

title: Annotate, do not rename, the Week 10 board columns (F-21)
problem: week10_signal_board.csv's 'closing_spread_home' column actually holds the AWAY team's spread (V8-verified), and 'market_implied_home_winprob' derives from an unvalidated formula.
proposal: Add a convention note and derived home-view column; leave original column names in place so existing consumers do not break. Exclude the implied-probability column from decision pages.
evidence: check V8 (data/verification-d.tsv); flag F26; the line board already negates per row and says so.
recommendation: A. Renaming breaks consumers; leaving it silently keeps misleading readers.
impact: Nobody reads the away spread as the home spread again.

title: Extend the verified results feed through the season in the weekly workflow
problem: The feed holds weeks 1-10. Backtests and ROI recompute as results land; nothing appends them automatically.
proposal: Wire scripts/build_results_feed.py and the standings cross-check into .github/workflows/refresh.yml so the feed extends weekly and fails loudly if the standings check breaks.
evidence: data/results_feed.json (137 rows); the build already proves 32/32 standings agreement.
prerequisites: Weekly official results capture (SG23 shares the plumbing)
recommendation: A. The verification is already automated; it should simply run.
impact: ROI and backtests stay current all season with the same provenance bar.

title: Fix the computed layer's break-even to use per-bet odds, then re-run its gates (F30)
problem: The computed-layer leaderboard's breakeven_hit is 1/(1+realized ROI), a circular quantity, so its G4 'beats_vig' gate is unusable and every strategy is failed by construction.
proposal: In scripts/strategy_lab.py, compute the hurdle from the odds already in the bet ledger (mean of 1/decimal odds across settled bets, or per-bet break-even), regenerate leaderboard.csv, and re-run the gate columns. A one-line change to avg_dec semantics plus a rebuild.
evidence: flag F30; data/leaderboard_signal_staking.json transcribes the wrong value with a warning rather than silently fixing another session's dataset.
reversibility: Reversible (git history holds the old build)
prerequisites: Owner acceptance that computed-layer verdicts may flip
options: Leave and read G4 as unusable.
Drop G4 from the computed layer.
recommendation: A. The odds are already in the ledger; the correct number is one line away.
impact: The computed leaderboard's gate columns become meaningful; the signal split can then rank against true price hurdles.

title: Choose canonical implementations of R21-R28 from the two parallel builds (F31)
problem: Two sessions independently implemented the eight requirements. Both are live on the site with different policy choices (market prices: strict blank vs badge-and-publish; demotion: D1-D3 vs G-14). A reader currently sees two answers to several requirements.
proposal: For each requirement, review both implementations (cross-linked on the affected pages) and pick one as canonical; move the other to archive/ with a note. Do not delete either: they are independent evidence about the same requirements.
evidence: flag F31; COORDINATION.md reconciliation record; line-board.html vs model-lines.html; verified-results-feed.html vs results-feed.html; validation.html (both gate sets).
options: Review pair-by-pair and pick per requirement. (Recommended)
Merge the best of both into one build now.
recommendation: A. This is the decision the Suggestions page exists for: two real options, one owner, one pass.
impact: The site answers each requirement once, with the losing implementation preserved as evidence.

title: Acquire one licensed odds feed and start open/close capture  (pairs with Q30 and SG16)
problem: The price-snapshot store is built and tested, but no verified price source exists, so the brief's open/close requirement cannot be filled (F18, Q21).
proposal: Choose one licensed feed (a commercial odds API, or a single designated book captured at fixed times), record open at market open and close at kickoff minus one minute per market, into engine/price_snapshots.py. The capture job is append-only and keyed to the model version.
evidence: price-snapshots.html; engine/price_snapshots.py; data/price_snapshots.csv (56 rows, opens blank).
risk: Low - the store rejects unattributed quotes, so a bad feed cannot silently pollute it.
reversibility: Fully reversible - the store is append-only; a withdrawn feed leaves its rows attributed and quarantined.
prerequisites: Q21 decision on source and terms
options: Commercial odds API subscription. (Recommended if budget exists)
Manual capture from one designated book at fixed times, documented per row.
Stay with closes only and say so on the page.
recommendation: A if the terms allow public display; otherwise B. Option C keeps the site honest but leaves opening-line movement unmeasurable.
impact: Fills the open columns, unlocks CLV and decay monitoring (D1), and lets validation gate G6 finally run.

title: Pre-register the demotion and promotion thresholds in one commit before any live stake  (pairs with SG17 and Q33)
problem: D1-D3 are implemented with documented default thresholds; defaults chosen in advance are proposals, but defaults left unfrozen can still be edited after a losing streak.
proposal: One commit, signed off, that freezes: the decay window, the calibration band, the concentration caps, the promotion gate list (G1-G6 all PASS) and the INSUFFICIENT_DATA floor. Review only on the gate-review schedule.
evidence: engine/demotion.py; validation.html; tests/test_requirements_core8.py.
reversibility: Reversible only by a later pre-registered amendment, never silently.
options: Freeze now with the documented defaults. (Recommended)
Wait for the first season's data to choose thresholds.
recommendation: A. Option B manufactures thresholds from results; option C reintroduces exactly the discretion the gates exist to remove.
impact: Makes demotion automatic and non-negotiable, which is the only version of it worth having.

title: Extend the results feed with player-level stats from an official source once one is identified  (pairs with Q34)
problem: Player-prop combos cannot be backtested from team-level results; the only player-level logs in the repo are third-party, so prop correlations stay blocked on the official-correlations page (CO-07).
proposal: Register an official player-statistics source (NFL.com gamebooks or the league's official statistics pages at season grain), capture it into an append-only feed like the results feed, and only then compute prop-pair correlations officially.
evidence: correlations-official.html (CO-07 blocked); prop-correlations.html (third-party estimates, labelled).
risk: Medium - official gamebooks are per-week documents; season-grain capture is real work.
options: Capture official gamebooks weekly into the feed. (Recommended)
Accept labelled third-party player logs for research, official-only for claims.
recommendation: A with B as the interim. C abandons part of the brief.
impact: Unblocks prop backtests, player-prop combos and CO-07 on official footing.

title: Schedule a weekly append-only capture of the injury report and depth charts  (weekly append captures)
problem: Everything on this site is one snapshot from 2026-11-14. A single snapshot cannot show practice-trajectory effects, week-over-week availability deltas (SIG-04), or any persistence claim.
proposal: A scheduled job (the repo already has a weekly refresh workflow) that appends the official injury report and each club's depth chart as dated, immutable snapshots, reconciling renders rather than overwriting (the report's row count varies between renders).
evidence: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md (one-snapshot blocker); data/injury_snapshot_b.json (two renders differ).
risk: Low - append-only; a bad capture is a new dated row, not a destructive edit.
options: Keep single snapshot and scope claims to Week 10.
recommendation: A. It is the cheapest way to turn a poster into a dataset.
impact: Unlocks within-season deltas, availability trend signals, and multi-week validation.

title: Decide the fair-line publication policy before the first fitted line ships  (pairs with Q31 and flag F20)
problem: The board publishes fair, market and difference as separate columns. Once a model exists, a policy is needed for whether a fair line publishes with an uncertainty band always, only after acceptance (Q22), or only alongside the naive baseline.
proposal: Fix the policy now: every published fair line carries its uncertainty band and the naive baseline beside it; unaccepted model output never reaches the board; sealed before kickoff.
evidence: line-board.html; line-origination.html (uncertainty section).
reversibility: Fully reversible until the first line ships; awkward afterwards.
options: Fair line always with band + baseline. (Recommended)
Fair line only after acceptance, without band.
Publish raw model output with a caveat.
recommendation: A. Option C is how invented numbers enter a site that promised never to publish them.
impact: Keeps the board's blank-cell promise intact once the model exists.

title: Adopt the decision-readiness table as the standing decision view (pairs with Q29)
problem: Every session publishes progress in its own pages; the owner must re-derive 'what blocks what' each time. The brief explicitly asks for a decision-readiness table on the landing page: one row per requirement, with the gate that blocks it and the number that would clear it.
proposal: Make data/readiness.json + readiness.html the canonical decision view; the landing page carries the compact table. Update it at every integration (statuses, gates, clearing numbers) instead of writing new parallel summaries.
evidence: index.html readiness section; readiness.html (28 requirements + 69-row brief audit).
options: Adopt as canonical, update at every integration. (Recommended)
Adopt but move the full brief audit off the site.
recommendation: A. One table beats five summaries; the brief asked for exactly this view.
impact: Every decision starts from the same table; drift between sessions' claims becomes visible immediately.

title: Automate official Game Center venue + Game Book capture in the weekly refresh
problem: The venue requirement ('transcribe the venue of every fixture from the official game centre') is met for 2/272 rows by hand this session; the remaining 270 stay labelled third-party. Game Books are confirmed reachable per game (the brief's Game Book requirement), but nothing captures them.
proposal: Extend .github/workflows/refresh.yml: for each game in the coming week (then rolling backfill), fetch the official Game Center page, record Location + Stadium + Game Book URL into a versioned register, and hash-pin the capture. Replaces the third-party Stadium label row by row.
evidence: data/venue_spotchecks.json (2 verified matches incl. Munich); both Game Centers expose Game Book PDF links.
options: Accept the labelled third-party column by decision.
recommendation: A. The access problem is solved; the remaining gap is one scheduled job.
impact: Turns D-23 and D-25 from partial into automatable; Game Books become the official starters source the brief wants.

title: Capture the 13 settled Week 10 finals and the reserve list at the next refresh run
problem: 13 Week 10 games are FINAL on the official page (verified 2026-11-16) but the committed feed snapshot holds blank scores (F43); the reserve-list capture (S70) is one month old the moment the next month starts.
proposal: At the next refresh run: transcribe the 13 finals row-by-row with official game links (the S61-S69 pattern), extend the verified results feed, and re-capture the current reserve-list month into a new dated file (never overwrite November).
evidence: F43; raw/nfl-reserve-list-2026-11.md; data/reserve_list_2026-11.tsv (25 rows).
options: Backfill immediately by hand in this session.
recommendation: A. Hand-editing feed rows outside the capture pipeline is exactly what the provenance rules forbid; the scheduled run is the right owner.
impact: Keeps the verified results feed and the reserve history current without breaking lineage.
